_note: Manual transcription of the Morse block on the address side (work/hires/cpc_--_USA__USA___adr.jpg), read from 3-5x enlargements. Card rows are given in order. Each word is a list of letters; each letter is its mark pattern: '.' dot, '-' dash, '=' long dash (American Morse L), a space inside a pattern is an internal (spaced-dot) gap. Commas drawn on the card are the word separators. Letters marked * in 'flags' rest partly on word sense (see SOLUTION.md).

flags.word 6 (I): two dots with intermediate gap (~60 hi-res px between centres; this writer's I elsewhere ~30, O ~90-105). Read I (I WILL); the card has no comma between I and WILL. O is not excluded by the pixels alone.
flags.word 7 letters 3-4 (WILL): the two dashes are ~95-100 px at display scale, between this writer's T (65-105) and L (145-150): read L L by word sense (WITT is not a word).
flags.word 9 letter 3 (SOON): the second O is written with a tight gap (~40 px), I-like; literally S O I N, transcribed as O by word sense.
flags.word 10 letter 2 (MY): two pairs of dots, the first pair wider than usual; read Y (.. ..); M + O + I is not a word.
flags.word 11 letter 3 (ADDRESS): the second D is written above the line and inserted with a caret by the writer.
